events.title: Ly Cong Uan ascends the throne
events.description: Ly Cong Uan, a native of Co Phap Village (now in Tu Son, Bac Ninh), ascended the throne as Emperor under the title Ly Thai To, founding the Ly Dynasty and ushering in a long period of prosperity for the country.

events.title: Construction of Phat Tich Pagoda
events.description: King Ly Thanh Tong ordered the construction of Phat Tich Pagoda (Van Phuc Pagoda) and a precious stupa on Lan Kha Mountain. This was a major Buddhist cultural center of Dai Viet at that time.

events.title: The battle on the Nhu Nguyet River defense line
events.description: Commander-in-Chief Ly Thuong Kiet led the army and people of Dai Viet to defeat the Song invaders on the banks of the Nhu Nguyet River (Cau River). Here, the poem 'Nam quoc son ha' resounded as the first declaration of independence.

events.title: Establishment of Bac Ninh Province
events.description: During the administrative reforms of King Minh Mang, Kinh Bac Town was renamed Bac Ninh Province. This was one of the first 13 provinces established in Tonkin.

events.title: French capture of Bac Ninh Citadel
events.description: French troops led by General Millot launched a major attack on Bac Ninh Citadel. The Nguyen Dynasty and Black Flag forces were defeated, and Bac Ninh Citadel fell to the French colonialists.

events.title: Establishment of the Bac Ninh Indochinese Communist Party Committee
events.description: At Hong Van Mountain (Lim Mountain), the Bac Ninh - Bac Giang Indochinese Communist Party Committee was established, marking an important development in the revolutionary movement of the Kinh Bac region.

events.title: Seizing power in Bac Ninh provincial capital
events.description: The Uprising Committee ordered the attack, and the masses from the districts flocked to Bac Ninh Town, disarming the Civil Guard, occupying the Resident's Office, and seizing power for the people.

events.title: The battle against the raid in Dinh Bang Village
events.description: The guerrillas and people of Dinh Bang fought resiliently, using a secret underground tunnel system to resist large-scale French sweeps, preserving their forces and inflicting casualties on the enemy.

events.title: Liberation of Bac Ninh Province
events.description: Following the defeat at Dien Bien Phu and the signing of the Geneva Accords, French troops withdrew from Bac Ninh Town. Regular troops and the people entered to take over, and Bac Ninh Province was completely liberated.

events.title: Fighting to defend Dap Cau Bridge
events.description: The army and people of Bac Ninh coordinated with air defense forces to fight fiercely to defend Dap Cau Bridge (a vital transportation artery) against destructive bombing raids by the US Air Force.

events.title: The Hoa Loc female militia battleground shooting down US aircraft
events.description: During the Dien Bien Phu in the Air campaign, militia and guerrilla forces of Tien Son and Yen Phong districts coordinated to shoot down US aircraft, contributing to the common victory of the army and people of the North.
